# Library Lending: business requirements document

Version 0.1.0 of the specification: why the system is built, for whom, and what the business asks of it, 4 stakeholders, 4 needs and 8 requirements, in the order of the business requirements specification of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148. How each requirement is designed and verified is in the requirements specification.

**Problems:** 4 warnings concern this document; each is marked by a Problem paragraph at its element, or below when the document shows no element for it. The problems file lists every problem, and specarch validate prints them.

## 1. Purpose and scope

A small public library lends books to its members. Members borrow a copy,
keep it for a fixed loan period, and pay a late fee when they return it
after the due date. This example exists to exercise every concept of the
meta-model in one place, across every stage of the life cycle; it is not
a real library's system.

Owners: example-maintainers.

No quality goal is written, so a trade-off is argued rather than decided. Add qualityGoals, three to five, each with rank, quality and statement.

## 6. Stakeholders

| Stakeholder | Who they are | Concerns |
|---|---|---|
| librarian | Staff at the desk who register members, lend copies and take returns. | Every desk task fits in one screen and takes under a minute; A fee is never wrong by a cent |
| member | A card holder who borrows books. | Only their own loans and fees are shown to them; They are told when a loan is overdue |
| library-board | The board that sets the lending policy and answers to the regulator. | The policy sheet and the system agree; Member data is kept as the rules allow and no longer |
| library-it | The library's IT staff, who build each release from the source and run production on the library's hosts. | A release can be built from the source alone, and the build compared with the vendor's; Every setting, port and host the system needs is written down before a release is installed |

## 7. Business needs

What the stakeholders said they need, the goals each need serves, and the requirements that refine it.

| Need | Statement | Stakeholders | Goals | Status | Refined by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NEED-1 | We need to know who has which copy and when it is due, without a card index. | librarian |   | accepted | LIB-1, LIB-3, LIB-7 |
| NEED-2 | We need late fees to be charged the same way for every member, as the policy says. | librarian, library-board |   | accepted | LIB-5, LIB-8 |
| NEED-3 | Members need to browse the catalogue without logging in, and to see only their own records when they do. | member, library-board |   | accepted | LIB-2, LIB-6 |
| NEED-4 | Members need to be told when a loan becomes overdue. | member |   | accepted | LIB-4 |

**Note on NEED-1:** From Interview with the desk staff about lending and returns: The card index is searched by hand when a member asks what they have out, and it is often out of date.

**Note on NEED-2:** From Lending policy of the library, 2026, clause 4: A late return is charged a flat daily rate, capped at the book's replacement cost.

**Note on NEED-3:** From The data-protection rules the library is bound by, 2024: Personal data is shown only to the person it is about and to the staff who need it.

## 8. Business requirements

Each requirement as the business asks it: its statement, how important it is, where it stands, the needs it refines and the goals those needs serve.

| Requirement | Statement | Priority | Status | Needs | Goals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LIB-1 | A member shall be identified by a unique card number and a unique email address. | must | accepted | NEED-1 |   |
| LIB-2 | Anyone shall be able to browse the catalogue without a card. | must | accepted | NEED-3 |   |
| LIB-3 | A member shall hold at most the number of open loans their tier allows, and shall not borrow while fees are outstanding. | must | accepted | NEED-1 |   |
| LIB-4 | A loan not returned by its due date shall become overdue the next day, and the member shall be told. | must | accepted | NEED-4 |   |
| LIB-5 | A late return shall be charged a flat daily rate, capped at the book's replacement cost. | must | accepted | NEED-2 |   |
| LIB-6 | A member shall see only their own loans and fees. | must | accepted | NEED-3 |   |
| LIB-7 | A desk task shall take a librarian under a minute, in one screen. | should | accepted | NEED-1 |   |
| LIB-8 | A late fee above the desk's limit shall be waived only after a second person, not the one who asked, approves it. | must | accepted | NEED-2 |   |

**Note on LIB-1:** From Lending policy of the library, 2026, clause 1: Each member holds one card, and the card number identifies them at the desk.

**Problem on LIB-2:** warning: scenario_uncovered: requirement LIB-2 has priority must and no step of any scenario names it, so no case shows it in sequence with the operations it runs through; add LIB-2 to the requirements of the scenario step that exercises it, or write a scenario for it [scenario_uncovered@requirements/requirements/lending.yaml#/requirements/LIB-2]

**Note on LIB-3:** From Lending policy of the library, 2026, clause 2: Standard members may hold three loans at a time and extended members six; no loan is made while a fee is unpaid.

**Open change request CR-1 on LIB-4:** Let a member renew a loan once. Raised in production by member on 2026-10-09; approved; cause omitted.

**Insight on LIB-5:** A flat rate can be checked by hand at the desk; the cap means a long-overdue book costs the same as a lost one, which is when the member should be told to treat it as lost.

**Note on LIB-5:** From Lending policy of the library, 2026, clause 4: The late fee is a daily rate set by the board, and never more than the cost of replacing the book.

**Note on LIB-6:** From The data-protection rules the library is bound by, 2024: Personal data is shown only to the person it is about and to the staff who need it.

**Problem on LIB-8:** warning: scenario_uncovered: requirement LIB-8 has priority must and no step of any scenario names it, so no case shows it in sequence with the operations it runs through; add LIB-8 to the requirements of the scenario step that exercises it, or write a scenario for it [scenario_uncovered@requirements/requirements/lending.yaml#/requirements/LIB-8]

**Insight on LIB-8:** A fee waived by the person who asked for it is money the library loses with nobody having looked; a second person is the control the board asks for.

## 9. Constraints

| Constraint | Kind | Statement |
|---|---|---|
| CON-1 | legal | Member data is kept only while the membership is open and for one year after, then deleted. |
| CON-2 | technical | Dates are the library's local calendar dates; timestamps are UTC. |

**Note on CON-1:** From The data-protection rules the library is bound by, 2024: Personal data is kept no longer than its purpose needs.

**Insight on CON-2:** A loan due on the 21st is overdue from the start of the 22nd, library time, whatever the server's clock.

## 10. Assumptions

| Assumption | Statement |
|---|---|
| ASSUME-1 | One library, one branch, one currency. |
| ASSUME-2 | The daily rate changes rarely and is a library setting, not a per-book value. |

**Note on ASSUME-2:** From Lending policy of the library, 2026, clause 4: The board sets the daily rate once a year.

## 11. Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| copy | One physical book. The example counts copies per title and does not identify them. |
| tier | A membership level that sets the loan limit and the loan period. |
| loan period | The number of days a copy may be kept; 21 for the standard tier, 28 for the extended tier. |
| late fee | The amount charged when a copy comes back after its due date. |
